claim.quote: improved spin-dependent weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP)-proton cross section limits by a direction-sensitive method were achieved including a new record of 5400 pb for 150 GeV/c2 WIMPs

key_value.note: Spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section limit at 150 GeV/c^2 (confidence level not stated in the abstract).
key_value.quote: a new record of 5400 pb for 150 GeV/c2 WIMPs

name: First underground results with NEWAGE-0.3a direction-sensitive dark matter detector

summary.plain: The first underground dark matter run of NEWAGE, in the Kamioka mine, gave improved direction-sensitive limits on how strongly dark matter could couple to protons, including 5400 pb for a 150 GeV/c^2 particle.
summary.technical: NEWAGE-0.3a, CF4 at 152 Torr, 20x25x31 cm^3 fiducial volume (0.0115 kg), exposure 0.524 kg d (2008-09-11 to 2008-12-04): spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 5400 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (direction-sensitive method).

title: First underground results with NEWAGE-0.3a direction-sensitive dark matter detector
why_it_matters: The abstract calls 5400 pb a new record for a direction-sensitive method at the time.
